description:
## Why
An agent that wants a new terminal already running a command has to create the surface and then `send`, and the send races shell startup. `new-workspace --command` does that race today and drops the queued result. Backlog item: C2.

## Evidence
- c11: `CLI/c11.swift:2213-2244` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e). `new-workspace --command` calls `workspace.create`, then `tab.send_text` with `unescapeSendText(commandText + "\\n")`, and discards the response (`:2241-2244`).
- c11: `new-split` (`:2247-2279`, method `tab.split`), `new-area` (`:2350-2377`, method `area.create`), and `new-tab` (`:2601-2623`, method `tab.create`) take cwd, title, and type. None takes `--command`. Help text at `:9010`, `:9137`, and `:9238` matches that.
- c11: `Sources/SocketHandlers/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:117-118` and `:232` pass `initial_command` into `addWorkspace` as `initialTerminalCommand`. That field replaces the shell. `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3689-3709` writes it to `surfaceConfig.command` inside `withCString` before `ghostty_surface_new`.
- c11: `ghostty.h:447-450` already has both `command` (shell replacement) and `initial_input` (typed into the interactive shell). Nothing in Swift assigns `initial_input`.
- Upstream: cmux #9614 (`7a0ba63056`). The CLI sends `initial_input = text + "\r"` on split, pane create, surface create, and workspace create. Non-terminal types are rejected. Blank text is dropped. The shell outlives the command.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1c. Fable row 4.3 (core). Astra row 4.3 raised the effort and marked it if-time. The backlog and `c11-1.0.html` revised decision keep it core.

## Scope
In: `--command` on `new-split`, `new-area`, and `new-tab`, carried as Ghostty `initial_input` with a trailing CR. Move `new-workspace --command` onto that same field. Reject it for browser and markdown. Drop blank text. Keep `initial_command` / `initialTerminalCommand` as the socket-only shell replacement.
Out: `launch-agent` prompt delivery (C11-258, and backlog C8). The bracketed-paste split (bug harvest #4). A delivery report that claims the command finished. `--command` together with `--layout` must not be invented as a second executor. Reject that pair with a clear error. The layout branch of `v2WorkspaceCreate` (`WorkspaceHandlers.swift:159-216`) returns before `initialTerminalCommand` is applied.

## Approach
Thread an `initial_input` string from the CLI through `tab.split`, `area.create`, `tab.create`, and `workspace.create`, and assign `surfaceConfig.initial_input` beside the existing `command` assignment, still inside a `withCString` that outlives `ghostty_surface_new`. Do not set `surfaceConfig.command` for this flag. Append `\r` in the app, not by reusing `unescapeSendText`, so a command that contains the two characters backslash-n stays literal. `new-workspace --command` stops calling `tab.send_text`. Return the created refs. Say in the human summary that the text was queued into the new shell, not that it ran. Update `skills/c11/references/api.md` and sync the installed c11 skill on the machine that lands the PR. Register feature flag `create.initial_input` if C6's list exists.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a tagged build, `c11 new-tab --command 'printf hi-from-create'` shows `hi-from-create` in that tab, and the shell is still alive afterwards (`echo ok` works). The same for `new-split down` and `new-area`.
2. `c11 new-tab --type browser --command 'echo no'` and the markdown equivalent exit with a usage error and open nothing.
3. `c11 new-workspace --command 'printf ws-create'` no longer issues `tab.send_text`. The text appears in the new workspace's terminal, and a slow shell rc does not lose it the way a follow-up send can. Record one run where rc output arrives before the command echo, and say whether the command still ran.
4. `c11 new-workspace --layout <name> --command 'printf x'` fails with an error that names both flags. No workspace is left behind, or the error says a workspace was not created.
5. A socket `workspace.create` with `initial_command` still replaces the shell. A fixture or existing test covers that, so the two fields stay distinct.

## Validation
A `tests_v2` script against a tagged build's socket for the four create verbs, plus one computer-use check that the new terminal is readable and still at a prompt. No soak. Ghostty buffers `initial_input` in the PTY before rc files finish. The acceptance run in criterion 3 is the check that this is livable. Do not add a retry loop that sends the command again.

## Dependencies
None. Related to C3: once this lands, `new-workspace --command` no longer has a `queued` send result to surface. C3 documents send. This ticket documents create. Feature flag name lives with C6.

## Risks
Typing latency: this runs at surface create, not per keystroke. Do not add a display link or a manual draw. Main thread: surface creation is already on the spawn path. Do not block the socket worker on rc completion. Doctrine: the command is spawn config for c11's own terminal. No shell rc writes, no tenant config. Localization: new CLI errors go through `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: nothing sensitive.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: the shell stays the shell. `--command` types into it.
title: Type --command into a new terminal via Ghostty initial_input
